examples.translation: to slow down one's pace; walk slower
examples.english: to slow down one's pace; walk slower

glosses: to hold back, to delay, to retard
делать более медленным, уменьшать скорость чего-либо

examples.text: Поезд стал замедлять ход. Замелькали предстанционные постройки и кирпичные теремки.
Однако накапливающиеся промежуточные продукты будут замедлять работу цикла, а лишний ацетил клетка использует для производства других веществ.
When approaching a bend in the road, slow down, and speed up after leaving it.
Crossing stations on single lines are laid out so that one line has a straight run through, and is signalled in each direction, avoiding the need to slow down to take the turnout into the loop.
When the long, hot journey drew to its end and the train slowed down for the last time, there was a stir in Jessamy’s carriage.
Then came the war... and everything slowed down.

glosses: To reduce the velocity, speed, or tempo of something.

examples.text: With a comfortable lead, the football team slowed down the tempo of the game.

A “moving platform” scheme[…]is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails.[…]This set-up solves several problems […]. Stopping high-speed trains wastes energy and time, so why not simply slow them down enough for a moving platform to pull alongside?
The elimination of vacuum-braked wagons would be slowed down, and the Western Region's flirtation with diesel-hydraulic locomotives was questioned.

glosses: To become less intense, enthusiastic, etc., usually with a positive connotation, implying that one is stripped of exaggerated or unnecessary eagerness.

examples.text: Whoa, slow down there, bucko. Everyone will get a chance. Be patient.

glosses: To reduce the velocity of something.

examples.text: In May, for example, the Illinois Central RR. introduced the long-expected streamline version of the Panama Limited, with diesel haulage, cutting the time over the 921 miles between Chicago and New Orleans by 2hr. to 18hr. each way—the fastest on record—but decelerated other trains over the same route.
The S.D.R. [Somerset & Dorset Railway] could not adhere to this schedule, and had to decelerate the service, but the original timings were restored when the M.R. and L.S.W.R. leased the S.D.R.

glosses: To reduce the rate of advancement of something, such as a disease.

examples.text: One of the disadvantages of increasing intermediate stops is that, as we have pointed out already, certain prestige trains have to suffer, notably the "Cornish Riviera Express", slowed 15min to Plymouth by stops at Taunton and Exeter; the "Torbay Express", decelerated 18min by stops at Reading, Westbury, Taunton and Newton Abbot; and the "Bristolian", which adds 14min in order to allow for a Bath stop and an increased load.

glosses: dafür sorgen, dass etwas die Geschwindigkeit verringert, dass es mit geringerer Geschwindigkeit vor sich geht

De koude berglucht had de lente op deze hoogte wat vertraagd, maar door de warmte liepen nu ook de bergbloemen allemaal uit.
